# DGXX: Behind-the-meter generation turns a 40 MW Cerebras contract into an AI revenue base above current revenue

## Bear case first
Insider conviction is the weak subscore: two insiders sold a net $-272M in the trailing 12 months (Form 4). The customer graph is thin, with one named enterprise customer and zero federal awards (USASpending). Colocation revenue fell in Q2 2026 versus Q2 2025 during the AI transition [10][11]. The filing warns of going concern and financing risk [16][19]. Missed phase dates [9] would delay or eliminate the contracted revenue.

## Business today
Four operating segments: cryptocurrency mining, energy sales, colocation services, and Tier III AI data centers [0][1]. Total revenue was $34.19MM and cash was $78.48MM as of 2025-12-31 (SEC XBRL). Colocation revenue was $6.45MM for the six months ended June 30, 2026 [13].

## Chain position
Node: data center operator and developer, first-order beneficiary, near-term horizon. Behind-the-meter generation bypasses utility interconnection queues, shortening time to power and letting data centers monetize capacity sooner. The Tier III AI data centers are the monetization asset [1].

## Customer graph
Enterprise: Cerebras Systems Inc., the sole named customer, under a 10-year agreement [3]. Government: $0 in federal awards (USASpending). Two other filers name the company (SEC XBRL). The filing does not attribute the reported colocation revenue to a named payer [13], so customer evidence is thin.

## Insider and management signal
Net open-market selling: $-272M across 2 buys and 6 sales by 2 insiders (Form 4). Management discloses specific terms: $195 per kW per month, 3% annual escalation, one-time construction payments, defined phase dates [4][8][9]. The filing states a transition from Bitcoin mining to AI infrastructure [5].

## Street view
Analyst count, consensus, and mean target are n/a, and no recent rating actions are available (Street view). Thin coverage is part of the setup.

## Non-linear case
If Phase 1 (15 MW) and Phase 2 (40 MW) hit their targets [9], the Cerebras contract implies roughly $93.6MM in annualized fees [4], against $34.19MM total revenue (SEC XBRL). AI segment assets grew from $11.02MM to $58.99MM in six months [2]. One-time construction payments [8] are unquantified, so the funding gap is an open question. The multiple outcome requires on-time construction, financing, and customers beyond Cerebras.

## Evidence
- Four operating segments, including colocation services and Tier III AI data centers [0][1].
- AI project assets: $11.02MM at 2025-12-31 to $58.99MM at 2026-06-30 [2].
- Ten-year colocation agreement with Cerebras signed 2026-05-04 [3].
- Take-or-pay fee of $195 per kW per month, escalating 3% annually; monthly fees $2.925MM and $4.875MM for Phase 1 and Phase 2 [4].
- Transition from Bitcoin mining to AI infrastructure [5].
- One-time construction payments for Phase 1 and Phase 2 [8].
- Phase 1 (15 MW) ready-for-service targeted at 2026-12-15; Phase 2 (40 MW) by end of first fiscal quarter 2027 [9].
- Q2 2026 colocation revenue $3.43MM, down from $4.49MM in Q2 2025, attributed to AI transition [10][11].
- Six-month 2026 colocation revenue $6.45MM [13].
- Going concern and financing risk disclosed [16][19].

## Sizing and survivability
About 8 trading days to build a position at $33.43MM average daily dollar volume (reality check). Net cash of $78.48MM and roughly 12.3 quarters of runway (reality check) are offset by share count up 207.1% in 12 months and a shelf registration on file (reality check). Dilution risk is active and warrants a staged entry.

## What would change our mind
A Form 4 with open-market insider purchases would reverse the negative signal. An 8-K or 10-Q reporting Phase 1 ready-for-service on or before December 15, 2026 would confirm execution. A second named customer in a 10-Q, or a federal award on USASpending, would reduce concentration risk.

# DUOT: On-site gas turbine fleets turn data center load growth into asset management fees outside utility capex

## Bear case first
The strongest disconfirming reading is that the Fortress program is already shrinking. New APR began scaling back the scope of services under the AMA [9], and the excerpts show no dated milestones such as design wins. Customer concentration is effectively one Fortress-related complex, New APR and Sawgrass. Insider open-market activity is zero (Form 4), and cash runway of about 0.6 quarters (reality check) means the company cannot outlast a slow ramp. No segment revenue breakdown is disclosed [6].

## Business today
DUOT sells asset management, sales, and operations services for mobile gas turbine fleets. Under the AMA, Duos Energy manages deployment and operations of a fleet of mobile gas turbines and balance-of-plant inventory [1][2]. Revenue is $27.0MM and cash is $1.9MM (SEC XBRL).

## Chain position
DUOT is the asset manager for behind-the-meter mobile turbine fleets, downstream of manufacturers but directly exposed to fleet deployment. It earns fees for managing capacity that bypasses utility interconnection queues, so revenue is levered to data center load growth, not utility T&D spending.

## Customer graph
Enterprise buyers: Fortress Investment Group, New APR, and Sawgrass APR Holdings LLC (customer graph). These three are one transaction complex, so the customer graph is effectively one enterprise relationship. Government buyer: $2.6MM in federal awards from the Department of Transportation (USASpending). One other filer names the company (customer graph). Customer evidence is concentrated, not broad.

## Insider and management signal
Form 4 shows net $0 in open-market trades over 12 months (Form 4), so insider conviction is absent. Management language is specific and committed: it names Fortress, New APR, and Sawgrass, and quantifies approximately 850 MW and 30 turbine generators [0][7]. The disclosure that New APR is scaling back the AMA scope [9] tempers that commitment.

## Street view
No sell-side coverage exists for this $323MM market cap, consensus n/a (street view). Thin coverage is part of the setup but also means no external validation.

## Non-linear case
The 850 MW under management [0] compares against $27.0MM revenue (SEC XBRL), so a small management fee per megawatt could be material relative to current revenue. If Fortress re-expands the AMA scope, or if DUOT signs similar asset management contracts with other turbine fleet owners, the fee stream could multiply. This requires data center operators to keep choosing on-site gas turbines over grid interconnection and DUOT to win repeat asset management contracts.

## Evidence
- In late 2024, the Company engaged with Fortress to assist in FIG's purchase of approximately 850 MW of electrical generation capacity, 30 mobile gas turbine generators [0][7].
- Under the AMA, Duos Energy manages the deployment and operations for a fleet of mobile gas turbines and balance-of-plant inventory [1][2].
- In December 2024, the Company entered into contracts with Fortress, and a $5.0MM cash advance was recorded as of December 31, 2024 [4].
- The Asset Management Services segment generates revenues through the AMA with New APR [6].
- New APR began scaling back the scope of services provided under the AMA [9].

## Sizing and survivability
Liquidity supports a small fund position: $10.5MM average daily dollar volume, about 24 trading days to build (reality check). Net cash is $1.9MM with cash runway of about 0.6 quarters (reality check), which threatens the thesis. Share count is up 62.1 percent in 12 months and a shelf registration is on file (reality check), so dilution risk is high.

## What would change our mind
- An 8-K or 10-Q disclosing a new or expanded asset management contract with a counterparty outside the Fortress complex.
- Form 4 filings showing insider open-market purchases.
- A USASpending federal award to DUOT for mobile turbine deployment, which would validate government demand.

# HYLN: A distributed generator for behind-the-meter data centers, not the utility standby revenue collector

## Bear case first
The grid capex flatline thesis benefits utility standby revenue, not Hyliion. Filings describe a generator with no named customer and no dated order milestone [0]-[9]. Cash was $22.938MM and runway is about two quarters (Reality check), so dilution is the base case. Federal awards fund development, not repeatable revenue (USASpending).

## Business today
Hyliion develops the KARNO Power Module, a distributed generator that differs from reciprocating engines and gas turbines [0] and targets 200 kW to low megawatts [3]. It is positioned for backup power, grid balancing, and microgrids with storage and renewables [4][5][6][7]. Revenue was $3.475MM and cash was $22.938MM as of 2025-12-31 (SEC XBRL).

## Chain position
Hyliion is an equipment supplier upstream of the order 3 node in the thesis, which is utility standby revenue. In the thesis, data centers with on-site generation retain a grid connection, creating standby fees, but Hyliion would earn from equipment sales, not fees. Locating the module near consumption avoids 5-10% transmission and distribution losses [1], supporting the behind-the-meter case.

## Customer graph
Federal awards total $22.880MM: Department of Defense $15.641MM, Department of Energy $6.000MM, and Department of Defense $0.999933MM (USASpending). These are government buyers. No named enterprise customer appears in the cited excerpts [0]-[9], and 0 other filers name Hyliion (Customer graph). Customer evidence is thin.

## Insider and management signal
No insider open-market purchases or sales appeared in the trailing 12 months (Form 4). Management is specific about the module [0][3] but does not disclose committed orders or quantified targets [0]-[9]. The absence of insider activity is neutral.

## Street view
Sell-side aggregators show unknown analyst count, consensus n/a, and mean target n/a (Street view). No firm rating actions are available. Thin coverage makes any future initiation a possible catalyst.

## Non-linear case
The non-linear path is from development awards to commercial orders. If KARNO becomes a standard backup or grid-balancing generator for data center microgrids, one program could require many modules and produce revenue far above the $3.475MM base (SEC XBRL). That requires cost, reliability, and emissions performance, plus named customers in the backup power [6] and grid balancing markets [7]. Government awards show technical credibility, not commercial scale.

## Evidence
- The KARNO Power Module is distinguished from systems that rely on reciprocating engines or gas turbines to drive a rotating shaft [0].
- Combined cycle gas turbine plants can exceed 50% efficiency but incur 5-10% T&D losses, which KARNO is expected to avoid by locating near consumption [1].
- Hyliion says KARNO is a distributed generation solution [2].
- Initial target applications are 200 kW to the low megawatt range [3].
- KARNO can integrate with energy storage and renewables [4].
- With storage and solar or wind, KARNO can enable microgrids for EV charging [5].
- The backup power market is well established and positioned to grow [6].
- The grid balancing and servicing market is expanding [7].
- Resiliency-as-a-Service and Virtual Power Plants are emerging business models [8].
- KARNO can offer a lower-emissions option for backup power if regulations tighten [9].

## Sizing and survivability
Market cap is $563MM, and about 10 trading days are needed to build a position at $25.335MM average daily dollar volume (Reality check). Net cash is $22.358MM and cash runway is about two quarters (Reality check). Share count rose 1.9% in 12 months and a shelf registration is on file (Reality check), so dilution risk is material.

## What would change our mind
A Form 4 showing an insider open-market purchase would signal conviction. A 10-Q or 10-K that names a commercial customer and order quantity would add validation. A USASpending award for production rather than development would extend the runway and opportunity.

# NWE: Flat T&D capex stalls rate base growth and turns the 2027 equity issuance into a dilution event.

## Bear case first
Flat T&D capex removes the rate base growth that allowed revenue depends on [8]; the name fails if that flat capex path is real. The disconfirming read is that management affirmed 2026 EPS guidance, targets 4-6% rate base growth, and named a merger partner [1][3], all of which could protect the stock and make the short fail. The filings do not show signed data center load commitments, so the growth plan is an open question. Insider selling is zero (Form 4), but customer evidence outside a small federal award is thin (USASpending).

## Business today
NWE sells regulated electricity and gas service in Montana and South Dakota; the Montana gas revenue requirement includes a step-down from gas production depletion [6], and South Dakota coal generation revenue is not easily identifiable due to bundled rates [7]. NWE is a fully regulated utility where rate base is the primary earnings driver [8]. Revenue was $414.265MM and cash was $8.781MM (SEC XBRL).

## Chain position
NWE occupies the rate-regulated electric utility node, order 1, at-risk, mid horizon. Rate base is the primary earnings driver [8]; the 2024 estimated rate base was $5.38 billion [0]. The company targets 4-6% rate base growth [1], and under flat T&D capex that is the vulnerable assumption.

## Customer graph
Government: $209,190 in federal awards from the Department of Health and Human Services (USASpending). Enterprise: no named enterprise customers appear in the evidence. Unproven: the remaining customer base is not tied to a named buyer, and two other filers name NWE (Customer graph), so the customer evidence is thin.

## Insider and management signal
No insider bought or sold NWE on the open market in the trailing 12 months, a net $0 signal (Form 4). Management language is specific: 2026 EPS of $3.68-$3.83, EPS growth of 4-6%, rate base growth of 4-6%, a $3.2 billion capital plan, equity issuances from 2027, FFO/debt of 14%, and a pending merger with Black Hills [1][2][3]. The targets are quantified, but no customer contracts support them.

## Street view
Sell-side aggregators show no analyst count, no consensus, and no target (Street view). No firm rating actions are available. The absence of a named rating leaves the stock under-covered, which means the short thesis is not being argued by visible sell-side voices.

## Non-linear case
The downside path starts if national T&D capex flatlines near $180 billion a year and data center load is served behind the meter. NWE then cannot add rate base for that load, and the 2027 equity issuance [2] lands when growth is stalling. If the Black Hills merger [3] closes on terms that dilute holders, or fails, EPS growth falls below the 4-6% guidance [1]. Coal generation provides only 7-8% of earnings [9], so coal performance cannot offset the shortfall. Each year of flat capex removes the next year's rate base growth, so the earnings gap compounds from a one-time miss into a multi-year shortfall.

## Evidence
- 2024 estimated rate base was $5.38 billion [0].
- Management affirmed 2026 EPS guidance of $3.68-$3.83, long-term EPS growth of 4-6%, rate base growth of 4-6%, and a $3.2 billion five-year capital plan [1].
- Equity issuances are expected to begin in 2027 to fund South Dakota generation investment; FFO/debt target is 14% [2].
- NWE and Black Hills announced a pending merger [3].
- Montana gas revenue requirement includes a step-down that approximates annual depletion of gas production assets in rate base [6].
- Coal generation rate base revenue is not easily identifiable due to bundled rates [7].
- NWE is a fully regulated utility where rate base is the primary earnings driver [8].
- NWE derives about 7-8% of earnings from jointly owned coal generation rate base [9].

## Sizing and survivability
A small fund can build a position in about 8 trading days at the stated liquidity (Reality check), but owning this stock is not supported by the thesis. Net cash was -$3,277.226MM and cash was $8.781MM (SEC XBRL), so the balance sheet is levered. The 2027 equity issuance [2] adds dilution risk, and share count rose 0.2% in the past 12 months (Reality check).

## What would change our mind
An 8-K reporting a state commission order that approves a rate base increase above the flat national trend would disconfirm the mechanism. A Form 4 showing open-market insider purchases would signal internal conviction. A 10-Q disclosure naming a data center as a counterparty would replace the unproven load assumption.

# MEI: Flat utility grid capex pushes a diversified electrical supplier into data center power

## Bear case first

Filings show no data center revenue, design wins, capacity commitments, or named customers. Quantified revenue movement is power distribution and lighting in off-highway and commercial vehicle markets [4]. Federal awards are $0 (USASpending), insider activity is $0 (Form 4), and net cash is -$185.4MM (reality check). The data center reference in [0] may be participation language, and the thesis fails if the contribution is immaterial against $1,019.2MM revenue (SEC XBRL).

## Business today

Methode sells power distribution products, including busbars, smart connect systems, battery disconnect units, and integrated circuit boards, plus user interface components, LED lighting, and sensors [1][2], and vehicle systems in the same categories [3]. Revenue was $1,019.2MM with cash of $139.6MM (SEC XBRL). Recent growth came from power distribution and off-highway lighting, offset by lower commercial vehicle lighting [4].

## Chain position

Methode is an order-2 beneficiary: a diversified electrical equipment supplier whose power distribution products [1] can serve data center electrical rooms, switchgear, and backup power. The mechanism is capacity utilization: flat utility T&D orders push factories to chase private data center contracts with similar content, and a broad product line offsets lost volume, though pricing is more competitive. The company names data center power infrastructure as a growth market [0].

## Customer graph

Enterprise buyers: none named. Government: federal awards $0, including Department of Defense $0 on contracts SPE7M224P3428 and N0010421PBC57 (USASpending). Three other filers name Methode, but not as customers. Data center buyers: unproven, with no contract, program, or revenue disclosure in [0].

## Insider and management signal

Form 4 shows no open-market insider buying or selling in 12 months, net $0 across 0 transactions (Form 4). Management names data center power infrastructure [0] but discloses no design wins, committed capex, or quantified targets. The absence of insider buying does not confirm conviction, and the language is participation, not commitment.

## Street view

Sell-side coverage is absent: analyst count unknown, consensus n/a, mean target n/a (street view). For a $498MM name, no coverage means the pivot is not in any visible estimate. Thin coverage is the setup, but also means no independent scrutiny.

## Non-linear case

Data center power becomes material if Methode converts busbar, BDU, and power distribution capability [1] into private contract wins. The non-linear path requires flat utility grid capex to force a lasting capacity reallocation, not a temporary order surge. If data center content per megawatt is large and Methode captures share, revenue shifts from cyclical vehicle markets to contracted projects, and the multiple re-rates. Required: a named design win, disclosed revenue, or capacity commitment.

## Evidence

- Growing participation in industrial growth markets, including data center power infrastructure [0].
- Power distribution capabilities include busbars, smart connect systems, battery disconnect units, and integrated circuit boards, plus user interface components, LED lighting, and sensors [1][2].
- The 10-K describes vehicle systems across power distribution, lighting, and sensors [3].
- Revenue increased on higher power distribution and off-highway lighting, offset by lower commercial vehicle lighting [4].
- The amended credit agreement prices multicurrency loans at floating rates plus 1.375% to 3.00% [5].

## Sizing and survivability

Average daily dollar volume is $11.1MM, about 23 trading days to build a position (reality check). Net cash is -$185.4MM (reality check), with a multicurrency credit agreement at floating rates [5]. Share count is down 0.6% (reality check), so dilution is minimal, but negative net cash limits flexibility.

## What would change our mind

A 10-K or 8-K disclosing data center revenue, a named customer, or committed capex. A Form 4 filing showing open-market insider buying. A federal award naming Methode in a data center power infrastructure project.

# ESP: Flat US grid capex strands a small T&D supplier with insider selling and no named orders

## Bear case first
The short fails if the flat grid capex thesis is wrong. The company carries $18.9MM in cash against a $189MM market cap, a cushion that limits downside. Federal awards of $18.7MM (USASpending) provide a revenue floor not tied to utility budgets, but they concentrate the customer base in one agency, and heavy insider selling of $1.7MM (Form 4) could be a completed de-risking event rather than a continuing signal. The stock is thinly traded at $2.9MM average daily dollar volume, and a small fund building a position over 84 trading days could face a liquidity squeeze.

## Business today
ESP sells power supplies, power converters, filters, power transformers, magnetic components, power distribution equipment, UPS systems, and antennas [0]. Revenue was $9.6MM and cash was $18.9MM as of 2025-06-30 (SEC XBRL). The customer base is primarily government, with no named enterprise customers in the evidence.

## Chain position
ESP occupies the transmission and distribution equipment supplier node. Utility capex is the primary demand driver for transformers, switchgear, and cable, so a flatline near $180B annually removes volume growth and leaves suppliers with idle fixed costs. The effect is direct because the company sells these product categories [0].

## Customer graph
Government is the proven buyer: federal awards total $18.7MM, including $10.1MM under Department of Defense contract 0002, $1.7MM under N6339419C0006, and $1.3MM under 0007 (USASpending). No named enterprise customers appear in the excerpts. One other filer names ESP. Customer evidence is thin beyond federal awards.

## Insider and management signal
Open-market insider activity is net $-1.7MM over 134 sales and zero buys in the trailing 12 months (Form 4). The 10-Q excerpt [0] is a product list only, with no management commentary on strategy, capacity, or orders. Absent insider buying or stated conviction, the signal is negative.

## Street view
Sell-side coverage is effectively absent: unknown analyst count, consensus n/a, mean target n/a. Thin coverage is itself a setup for an at-risk name, but it also means no sell-side pressure is forcing the stock lower.

## Non-linear case
The non-linear path is the short working. Utility T&D capex flatlines, order volumes fall, and ESP's fixed cost base produces margin compression. Revenue declines toward the federal award floor, cash burns, and the company issues equity to fund operations; the 7.1 percent share count increase in 12 months (SEC XBRL) already shows dilution appetite. A multi-year decline with repeated offerings can take the stock to net cash value and below.

## Evidence
- ESP's primary products are power supplies, power converters, filters, power transformers, magnetic components, power distribution equipment, UPS systems, and antennas [0].

## Sizing and survivability
A small fund can own this: $2.9MM average daily dollar volume requires about 84 trading days to build a full position (Reality check). Net cash of $18.9MM (SEC XBRL) funds operations, but the share count is up 7.1 percent in 12 months (Reality check), so dilution risk is live. The cash cushion protects the balance sheet, not the thesis.

## What would change our mind
- A named customer contract in a 10-Q, 10-K, or 8-K filing showing enterprise orders outside federal awards.
- Insider open-market buys on Form 4 reversing the 134-sale pattern.
- A federal award large enough relative to the $9.6MM revenue base to prove a new demand source (USASpending).

# SLNH: Behind-the-meter solar and storage integrator should benefit if data center on-site generation grows while utility T&D capex stays flat.

## Bear case first

The bear case is that Soluna is a micro-cap cash consumer with no visible customer pipeline. The 10-K language describes a development approach, not a contracted backlog, and the only federal awards are $14.45M combined (USASpending). Insider open-market sales netted -$649.219M over 12 months (Form 4), and the share count rose 711.4 percent in the same period (SEC XBRL), pointing to dilution rather than value creation. Revenue is $29.717MM, but net cash is -$17.437MM and cash runway is about 0.2 quarters (SEC XBRL). Flat utility capex could also mean fewer transmission opportunities and less demand for any grid-adjacent developer.

## Business today

Soluna builds behind-the-meter generation at renewable sites, using on-site generation and existing grid interconnection infrastructure to improve power economics and accelerate timelines [0]. It bypasses long interconnection queues and sources electricity directly from the generation site [1]. Revenue was $29.717MM and cash was $462M as of 2025-12-31 (SEC XBRL).

## Chain position

In the seed thesis, Soluna occupies the behind-the-meter solar and storage integrator node. Each data center project bundles modules, inverters, and batteries, so integrator revenue rises with project count. Behind-the-meter projects avoid transmission costs and interconnection queues, making them faster to deploy than grid-connected renewables.

## Customer graph

Customer evidence is thin. Enterprise buyers: none named. Government buyers: federal awards total $14.45M, with the Department of Veterans Affairs at $10.69M and the Department of Defense at $3.76M (USASpending). One other filer names Soluna, which counts as an unproven buyer.

## Insider and management signal

Trailing 12-month Form 4 open-market activity is net -$649.219M, from 3 buys and 30 sales by one insider (Form 4). That is selling. Management language cites better power economics, faster timelines, and queue avoidance [0][1], but the excerpts contain no named programs, capital commitments, or quantified targets.

## Street view

Consensus is n/a, the mean target is n/a, and no analyst firm is listed in the aggregator data. Reports are paywalled and not linked. For a micro-cap with thin sell-side attention, the lack of coverage is part of the setup.

## Non-linear case

The non-linear case relies on the seed thesis: data center load growth is met by on-site gas turbines and solar plus storage behind the meter, keeping utility T&D capex flat. Soluna would be an order-1 beneficiary as project volume rises. Each behind-the-meter project bundles modules, inverters, and batteries, so revenue scales with installed units. To deliver a multiple, Soluna must convert its development approach into named customer contracts and positive cash flow. The filing excerpts do not currently show that pipeline.

## Evidence

- By building behind the meter at renewable generation sites, Soluna accesses on-site generation and existing grid interconnection infrastructure, which can improve power economics and accelerate development timelines [0].
- Behind-the-meter development bypasses long interconnection queues and sources electricity directly from the generation site [1].

## Sizing and survivability

Average daily dollar volume is $22.177MM, so a fund would need about 12 trading days to build a position (reality check). Net cash is -$17.437MM and cash runway is about 0.2 quarters (reality check). The share count rose 711.4 percent in 12 months and a shelf registration is on file (reality check), so dilution is a live risk.

## What would change our mind

- A named customer contract for a behind-the-meter solar or storage project would appear in a 10-Q, 10-K, or 8-K.
- A Form 4 open-market buy by an insider after 12 months of net selling.
- A federal award above $1MM from the Department of Energy or Department of Defense, visible in USASpending.

# ARRY: Tracker supplier with no offset to behind-the-meter margin compression

## Bear case first
The short fails if tracker hardware pricing holds while integrator margins compress. ARRY sells solar tracking technology to utility-scale and distributed generation customers [0][1], and the at-risk node is downstream integrator margin, not equipment pricing. The dossier shows no insider selling (Form 4), removing a confirmation signal for the short. Customer evidence is thin, with only $2.2MM in federal awards (USASpending), which weakens a bearish concentration argument but also leaves the revenue base unvalidated. The closest filing link to the theme is the EPC flow-down clause risk in [3], which is a contractual risk, not proven margin erosion.

## Business today
ARRY is a global provider of solar tracking technology and fixed-tilt systems to utility-scale and distributed generation customers who construct, develop, and operate solar PV sites [0][1][4]. Revenue was $1,284MM and cash was $244MM as of 2025-12-31 (SEC XBRL). The company says its cost advantage drives adoption across distributed generation and utility-scale markets [2].

## Chain position
ARRY sits at the equipment supply node upstream of the at-risk behind-the-meter integrator node. The theme's mechanism is integrator margin compression as capital floods into behind-the-meter solar and storage; ARRY gets paid for trackers regardless of the integrator's profit per project, so the pass-through is indirect. The node is order 3 with a long horizon, meaning the pressure compounds slowly and may take years to reach tracker pricing.

## Customer graph
Enterprise: none named in the excerpts (unproven). Government: $2.2MM in federal awards, all from the Department of Defense (USASpending). No other filers name the company. The customer graph is thin and provides no anchor buyer, which is consistent with a broad market but leaves the revenue base unverified.

## Insider and management signal
No open-market insider buying or selling in the trailing 12 months, net $0 across 0 buys and 0 sales by 0 insiders (Form 4). Management language is generic business overview and risk factors; the only theme-relevant statement is the disclosure that EPCs may impose flow-down clauses making subcontractor obligations identical to the EPC's obligations to its end customer [3]. There is no commitment to named programs or quantified targets.

## Street view
Sell-side coverage is unmeasured: unknown analyst count, consensus n/a, and mean target n/a per aggregators. For a $704MM market cap small-cap, absent coverage means the short is not crowded but price discovery is poor. No firm rating actions are available.

## Non-linear case
The short compounds if integrator margin compression spreads upstream to hardware pricing. If data center load is met by on-site gas turbines rather than solar-plus-storage, tracker demand stalls and the $1,284MM revenue base contracts. Flow-down clauses in [3] become the mechanism: EPCs pass concessions to subcontractors, and ARRY accepts thinner margins to hold volume. The negative net cash position of $-184MM (SEC XBRL) turns a revenue decline into a liquidity event, and the 1% annual share count creep accelerates if equity is issued.

## Evidence
- [0] 8-K filed 2026-08-20: transaction expected to close in Q3 2026; company described as leading global provider of solar tracking technology and fixed-tilt systems.
- [1] 10-K filed 2026-02-25: business overview, leading global provider of solar tracking technology and fixed-tilt systems to utility-scale and distributed generation customers.
- [2] 10-K filed 2026-02-25: cost advantage drives adoption across distributed generation and utility-scale markets.
- [3] 10-K filed 2026-02-25: risk from EPC flow-down clauses that make subcontractor obligations identical to the EPC's obligations to the end customer.
- [4] 10-K filed 2026-02-25: overview, same description as [1].

## Sizing and survivability
At $44MM average daily dollar volume, building a position takes about 6 trading days (Reality check), which is feasible for a small fund but leaves the short exposed during accumulation. Net cash is negative at $-184MM (SEC XBRL), so an equity raise is plausible and could cause a short-covering bounce. The 1% share count increase (Reality check) is mild dilution but signals that management will issue stock if cash runs short.

## What would change our mind
- Form 4 open-market insider purchases by officers or directors, which would contradict the avoid stance.
